question: Hoarseness persisting for more than three weeks in an adult is a red-flag symptom that mandates laryngoscopic examination to exclude laryngeal malignancy, regardless of the clinical context.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Any adult with hoarseness lasting more than three weeks must have laryngoscopy — the vocal cords cannot be assessed without direct or indirect visualisation, and early glottic carcinoma is curable.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The >3-week rule is the standard ENT safety-net for adult hoarseness. Delayed laryngoscopy is a common cause of late diagnosis of glottic carcinoma.
